one_liner: Rust SAM/BAM sorter packaging fgumi's external merge-sort engine; claims about 1.9x over samtools sort in template-coordinate order.
what_it_does: mako is a single-purpose CLI that sorts SAM/BAM by coordinate, queryname (lexicographic or samtools-style natural) or template-coordinate, and can check sortedness in one streaming pass with --verify. It is a 72-line wrapper: main.rs flattens fgumi's `sort` command (fgumi 0.7.0) and sets mimalloc as the global allocator, so every option and default is fgumi's. Inputs and outputs are files or stdin/stdout via -i/-o; it can write a .bai for coordinate output.
how_it_is_fast: The fgumi-sort engine packs each record's order into a precomputed sort key, sorts in-memory chunks with a parallel radix sort (voracious_radix_sort, an MSD hybrid for template-coordinate keys) and merges spilled runs with a loser tree, so merge comparisons are fixed-width key compares rather than record decodes. BGZF goes through libdeflate (C, via libdeflater), spill files use zstd level 1 instead of BGZF, input is prefetched with an adaptive number of positional reads, and spilled-run consolidation is sized from `ulimit -n` so the final k-way merge usually skips a rewrite pass. Release builds use fat LTO and codegen-units=1.
when_to_use: Template-coordinate sorting before UMI grouping or deduplication (fgumi group/dedup), where samtools sort --template-coordinate also ignores the tc tag on secondary and supplementary reads.
Large WGS BAMs that spill to disk on a box with a generous open-file limit and fast or several temp volumes (-T is repeatable).
Pipelines that pipe sorted output straight into another tool: --compression-level 0 writes stored BGZF with no DEFLATE.
Checking whether a BAM is already sorted without rewriting it (--verify).
when_not_to_use: When you need a measured, reproducible win over samtools: the only number is one README sentence with no hardware, thread count, memory limit, samtools version or command.

As a literal command-line drop-in for `samtools sort in.bam -o out.bam`: input needs -i, the default order is template-coordinate (not coordinate), and plain `queryname` is lexicographic, not samtools -n natural order.
When output size matters and you keep defaults: output is BGZF level 1 by default versus htslib's level 6, so files are larger unless --compression-level is raised.
If you want a stable, independently maintained engine: mako has 9 stars and 0 forks, all sort logic lives in fgumi (pre-1.0, APIs may change), and engine bugs are routed to the fgumi tracker.

integration.form: CLI binary (crate fg-mako, Bioconda fg-mako, prebuilt Linux and macOS binaries); the engine is usable as the fgumi-sort library crate
integration.dependencies: fgumi 0.7.0 (fgumi-sort, noodles, rayon, crossbeam, voracious_radix_sort), libdeflate via libdeflater (C), zstd (C libzstd), mimalloc (C), clap, env_logger
integration.platforms: Linux and macOS on x86_64 and aarch64 (release binaries); other targets not documented
integration.thread_safety: not applicable (CLI); --threads (default 1), --sort-threads and --merge-threads control the internal pools, and the output is byte-identical across thread splits per the help text
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same sort orders, a samtools-like 768M-per-thread memory default and 1-thread default, but different flags (-i/-o), a template-coordinate default order, lexicographic queryname by default, and output compression level 1 instead of 6

gotchas: Unequal default work behind the 1.9x claim: mako/fgumi write output at libdeflate level 1 (CompressionOptions default_value_t = 1), while samtools sort leaves htslib's default (level 6; bgzf.c maps -1 to 6 for libdeflate) and spills at level 1; temp spills are zstd level 1 in mako. The command behind the 1.9x is unpublished, so a default-versus-default run would credit cheaper output compression to the sorter.

The compared outputs are not the same order for every record: fgumi's best-practices.md says samtools sort --template-coordinate does not consult the tc tag for secondary and supplementary reads and is not a substitute; fgumi's CI (PR #577) only gates sort correctness against an unpinned apt samtools, tie-insensitively, and records no timings.
Running mako without --order produces template-coordinate output, and --write-index is accepted only for coordinate order to a seekable file.

CRC32 checking is on for file input and off by default for stdin; the engine is being refactored (the legacy sort path was removed for fgumi 0.8.0, where a release candidate briefly stopped enforcing --max-temp-files, issue #991, fixed before release; mako 0.1.7 is on 0.7.0 and unaffected).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The closest sibling for this job is sambamba (D), whose catalogued CRG comparison has samtools winning on sort; pick mako when you need template-coordinate order or a currently maintained spill-to-disk sorter, and keep samtools when compatibility with existing scripts and default output size matter more than a speedup that has never been published with methodology.
verified_claims_summary: A single first-party sentence says the engine sorts a 30M-read WGS BAM into template-coordinate order about 1.9x faster than samtools sort; no hardware, thread count, memory limit, samtools version, compression level or command is given anywhere in mako or fgumi, and the two tools' defaults differ in output compression level (1 vs 6).
status_note: Active (0.1.7 on 2026-08-25, tracking fgumi releases; MIT; 198 crates.io downloads) and easy to install through cargo or Bioconda, but it is a thin wrapper over a fast-moving pre-1.0 engine and its speed claim is unreproducible and possibly inflated by a lower default output compression level.
